setup_summary.text: P&G reports fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ending Dec 31, 2026) on 2027-01-20 before the open. Consensus is EPS $1.88 and revenue $23.50B, which implies +5.6% EPS and +5.8% revenue growth against $1.78 and $22.21B a year earlier. The EPS base is GAAP diluted EPS. We could not confirm whether the $1.88 consensus is GAAP or core.

Q1 FY27 (reported Oct 22) was a clear beat. Net sales were $23.28B (+4.0%), with organic +4.0% on volume +2.4%, mix +1.1% and price +0.4%. Core EPS was $2.00 (+1%) and diluted EPS was $1.97 (+1%). The Street expected core EPS of about $1.88-1.89 and revenue of about $22.7-22.8B, and the stock rose about 6% on the day.

The Q1 beat came against a management warning on the Q4 call that Q1 EPS would be down 5% or more. Actual diluted and core EPS were each up 1%. Pre-print consensus of about $1.88 was consistent with that warning. The guide proved conservative, but the Q1 gross margin still fell 160bp to 49.8% (140bp from commodities). Operating margin fell 70bp to 25.5%. EPS growth came from SG&A leverage, a lower share count and sales growth, not from margin.

FY27 guidance was held at organic sales +1% to +3% and core EPS $6.89-$7.11 (0% to +3%). All-in sales growth was raised to 2%-4% from 1%-3% to reflect Thorne. The commodity cost headwind was raised to about $1.4B after tax from about $1B. That makes the remaining three quarters easier than the first on paper, but they still need about +2% core EPS growth at the midpoint.

The Q2 setup combines three things. The cost headwind is first-half weighted, because materials were produced when oil was above $100. Thorne ($3.9B, closed Oct 1) is included for the first time. Funding costs are higher: net short-term borrowing of $5.8B in Q1 and a $4.0B bond deal on Oct 30 at 5.125%-5.900% coupons.

Peer read-across is mixed. Colgate's North America volume fell 3.7% in Q3, and Kimberly-Clark's North America organic sales fell 0.7% in Q2. Both cite oil-linked input inflation. P&G's Q1 volume of +2.4% runs against that backdrop, which raises the question of how repeatable it is.

last_reported.text: Q1 FY27 net sales were $23.28B (+4.0% y/y). The year-ago Q2 base is $22.21B.

consensus.text: Consensus is $23.50B, or +5.8% y/y. That is above Q1's +4.0%, above the FY27 organic range of 1-3% and at or above the top of the all-in range of 2-4%.

view.text: Bridge from guidance, using our own rough arithmetic: organic growth of about 2-4% on $22.21B gives about $22.7-23.1B. Add Thorne at roughly $0.3B a quarter (the one-point lift in the all-in range on $87.03B of FY26 sales, spread over three quarters). That gives about $23.0-23.4B, so $23.50B looks at or above the top of the range unless FX or volume surprises. Thorne's actual contribution is not disclosed.

last_reported.text: Q1 organic sales were +4.0% on volume +2.4%, price +0.4% and mix +1.1%. FY26 organic was about +1%, with the second half about 2 points stronger than the first.

view.text: FY27 guidance is organic +1% to +3% and assumes about 2% category growth, with a 30-50bp restructuring headwind. Q1's 4.0% is well above that. Q4 FY26 sell-in (-1%) lagged consumption (+2%) because of destocking, so Q1 may have included some rebuild. The 10-Q does not say so. Watch whether Q2 organic stays above 3%. A drop to 2-3% would match guidance and is not a miss.

last_reported.text: Q1 gross margin was 49.8%, down 160bp: commodities -140bp, product and packaging investment -140bp, mix -50bp and restructuring -10bp. Offsets were productivity +120bp, tariff costs and recoveries +50bp and pricing +20bp.

view.text: This is the main swing factor. Management says most of the cost headwind lands in the first half, and the commodity headwind estimate was raised to about $1.4B. The 50bp tariff benefit may not repeat, since only about half of the roughly $200M of IEEPA tariffs paid had been recognized as recoverable by Q4. Expect a year-on-year decline of similar size or larger, offset by productivity. Peers show raw-material headwinds largely absorbed by savings and pricing.

last_reported.text: Q1 SG&A was flat at $5.7B and 24.3% of sales (-90bp). Operating margin was 25.5% (-70bp). Overhead fell 70bp as a share of sales and marketing fell 20bp as a share of sales, even though marketing spend rose in dollars.

view.text: Half the 7,000 overhead role cuts are done and savings should keep flowing. Management says it stays fully invested in media. Peer Colgate raised advertising 15% to 14.4% of sales. Watch whether marketing keeps rising in dollars into the holiday quarter and whether SG&A leverage again carries operating profit.

last_reported.text: Q1 diluted EPS was $1.97 and core EPS $2.00 (restructuring add-back $0.03). Year-ago Q2 diluted EPS was $1.78.

consensus.text: Consensus is $1.88, +5.6% against the GAAP $1.78 base. It sits $0.12 below Q1 core EPS, consistent with a cost-heavy first half. Simply Wall St reported no meaningful change in earnings estimates after Q1.

view.text: To reach the $7.00 core EPS midpoint after Q1's $2.00, the remaining three quarters need $5.00 against $4.90 last year, about +2%. The low end of $6.89 implies roughly flat and the high end of $7.11 about +4%. Q2 FY26 GAAP EPS likely carried incremental restructuring, so a +5.6% headline may overstate core growth. The Q2 FY26 core EPS base is not in our sources.

metrics_to_model.metric: Net interest expense and other non-operating income

last_reported.text: Q1 interest expense was $223M (+$26M), interest income $102M (-$6M) and other non-operating income $207M (-$61M).

view.text: FY27 guidance already includes about $150M after tax of higher net interest expense and $150M of lower non-operating income. Coupons on the new $4.0B of notes sum to about $220M a year pre-tax (about $55M a quarter at full run-rate). The notes closed Oct 30, so Q2 carries about two months. The 10-Q says Q1 financing was a net debt increase related to the planned Thorne acquisition. Interest could step up again in Q2 and Q3.

last_reported.text: The Q1 effective tax rate was 21.0% against 20.8%, driven by discrete uncertain-tax-position items.

view.text: Guidance is a core tax rate of about 20% for FY27. A 21% print is within noise but costs about 1% of EPS.

metrics_to_model.metric: Operating cash flow, capex and free cash flow

last_reported.text: Q1 operating cash flow was $5.77B, capex $1.37B (5.9% of sales) and free cash flow $4.40B (93% of net earnings). A $1.15B payables inflow helped, and about $6.5B of payables sits in supply-chain finance.

view.text: FY27 guidance is capex of 4.5-5.5% of sales and adjusted FCF productivity of 85-90%. Q1 capex ran above that range and Q1 cash conversion was helped by payables. Expect productivity to fall toward guidance as payables normalize and Thorne integration and restructuring cash costs flow through.

last_reported.text: Q1 diluted weighted shares were 2,407.2M against 2,436.8M. P&G bought $1.25B of stock (about 11.5M shares at an average $146.47 including plan-related purchases).

view.text: Guidance is about $5.0B of direct repurchases in FY27, financed partly by debt. A share count down about 1% year on year adds about 1 point to EPS growth, as in Q1. Stock-option dilution has fallen (17.0M vs 25.3M).

guidance.guidance: +1% to +3% vs prior year, including a 30-50bp headwind from brand, product-form and go-to-market discontinuations. Assumes category value growth of about 2%.

claim.text: P&G kept FY27 organic sales growth guidance at +1% to +3% on Oct 22, including a 30-50bp discontinuation headwind. The Q4 call framed the midpoint as about 2% market growth plus share gains.

guidance.guidance: +2% to +4% vs prior year, up from +1% to +3% to reflect the Thorne acquisition.

claim.text: All-in sales growth guidance was raised to 2%-4% to reflect the Thorne acquisition as of Oct 1, 2026.

guidance.guidance: 0% to +3% growth on FY26 core EPS of $6.89, i.e. $6.89-$7.11 with about $7.00 at the midpoint.

claim.text: FY27 core EPS guidance of $6.89-$7.11 was reiterated on Oct 22 despite the larger commodity headwind.

guidance.guidance: +1% to +5% growth versus FY26 diluted EPS of $6.62.

claim.text: FY27 diluted EPS growth guidance was maintained at +1% to +5%.

guidance.metric: Commodity, energy and transport cost headwind
guidance.guidance: About $1.4B after tax, up from about $1B. Assumes Brent near $90 and is weighted to the first half. This is a larger cost headwind, not an improvement.

claim.text: The commodity cost headwind estimate rose to about $1.4B after tax from about $1B (the Q4 call figure), yet core EPS guidance was held. The Q4 call described Brent at $90 and cost pressure concentrated in the first half.

guidance.metric: Below-the-line items (FX, net interest, non-operating income, tax)
guidance.guidance: About $50M after-tax FX headwind, about $150M higher after-tax net interest, about $150M lower after-tax non-operating income, and a core tax rate of about 20%. The Oct 22 materials total all headwinds at $0.79 per share (11% of core EPS growth) against $0.56 (8%) on the Q4 call.

claim.text: The Q4 call put total input-cost, FX and below-the-line headwinds at about $1.4B, or $0.56 per share (8% of FY26 core EPS). A post-Q1 report cites $0.79 per share and an 11% drag. The two are not reconciled in our sources. The newer Oct 22 figure is the same type of evidence (guided) and should be preferred. The call's total of $1.4B is not the same as the newer commodity-only $1.4B.

guidance.metric: Capex and adjusted free cash flow productivity
guidance.guidance: Capex 4.5%-5.5% of sales. Adjusted FCF productivity 85%-90%. The long-term algorithm is 90% or more.

claim.text: The Q4 call set FY27 capex at 4.5-5.5% of sales and adjusted FCF productivity at 85-90%. No update was found in the post-Q1 sources. Q1 capex ran at about 5.9% of sales.

guidance.guidance: Dividends over $10B and about $5.0B of direct share repurchases, about $15B returned in total. Repurchases are expected to be financed partly by debt.

claim.text: The 10-Q says the Oct 22 earnings release reaffirmed about $5.0B of FY27 repurchases, financed by operating cash flow and debt issuance. Dividends of over $10B were part of the Q4 call outline.

guidance.guidance: About $2.0B pre-tax over two years, with the remainder in FY27, and up to 7,000 non-manufacturing roles cut by end of FY27. Q1 charges were $192M pre-tax.

claim.text: The restructuring plan is unchanged at about $2.0B pre-tax over two years, with Q1 charges of $192M. Charges above the ongoing $250-500M a year are excluded from core EPS.

since_filing.text: On Oct 30 P&G closed a $4.0B public notes offering: $750M 5.125% due 2031, $750M 5.300% due 2033, $1.25B 5.450% due 2036 and $1.25B 5.900% due 2056. The coupons compare with a 3.3% weighted average on long-term debt at June 30. The notes sum to about $220M a year of coupon pre-tax. The Sept 30 balance sheet already showed $17.0B of debt due within one year, and Q1 net additions to other short-term debt were $5.8B.

The 10-Q and the Oct 22 release postdate the Q4 call. Contradiction on Q1: the call guided Q1 EPS down 5% or more (undated, older), while the 10-Q (Oct 22, newer, reported) shows diluted EPS +1% and core EPS +1%. The reported figures take precedence. Also, the call guided organic growth of 1-3% for FY27, while Q1 organic was +4.0%.

Contradiction on costs: the Q4 call described a total FY27 headwind of about $1.4B after tax ($0.56 per share) made up of about $1B of input costs plus FX, interest and non-operating items. Post-Q1 reports say the commodity headwind alone is now about $1.4B, up from about $1B, and that combined headwinds are $0.79 per share (11% of core EPS growth). The newer reports are the same evidence tier (guided) and prevail. Core EPS guidance was held.

Contradiction on Thorne: the 10-K (Aug 4) said it would close in fiscal Q2 for $3.8B subject to approval. The 10-Q (Oct 22, newer) says it closed Oct 1 for $3.9B in cash, so Thorne is already in the base for the quarter ahead. The Q4 call did not mention it.

Sell-side targets rose after Q1 without earnings upgrades. Citi $187 (Buy), JPMorgan $180 (Overweight), BNP Paribas Exane $189 (Outperform), Morgan Stanley $185 (Overweight), Barclays $165 (Equal Weight), Piper Sandler $167 (Neutral), Goldman $161 (Neutral) and Bernstein $149 (Market Perform). Simply Wall St put the consensus target at about $173, up 7.2%, with no meaningful change to earnings estimates. MarketBeat counts 15 Buy and 11 Hold ratings.

Peers reported since the 10-Q. Colgate (Oct 30) raised 2026 adjusted EPS growth to 5-7%, with North America sales -1.7% on volume -3.7% and a 300bp raw-material headwind offset by savings and price. Colgate expects category softness to continue through 2026. Kimberly-Clark's Q2 10-Q cites about $150M of incremental oil-linked input costs for the rest of 2026.

P&G has an Investor Day on Nov 19 in Cincinnati, before the Jan 20 report. Colgate-Palmolive Pakistan also agreed on Oct 28 to buy P&G Pakistan's Karachi plant and land, subject to competition approval. That is part of ongoing footprint pruning and is unlikely to be material.

key_debates.question: Is Q1's 4.0% organic growth a new run rate or a one-off helped by retailer restocking and timing?

bull.text: Volume was +2.4%, Fabric & Home Care share rose 0.3pt, Baby Care share rose 0.8pt and Grooming share rose 0.2pt. Management says the share of top US customer-brand combinations holding or growing share rose from under 10% to about 50%. Interventions land in July-December, and Q4 consumption (+2%) was above sell-in (-1%).

bear.text: FY27 guidance is still 1-3% and assumes about 2% category growth. A peer's North America volumes fell 3.7%. Only 23 of the top 50 category-country combinations held or grew share in Q4. Share fell in Skin Care (-0.6pt), Personal Care (-0.4pt), Oral Care (-0.6pt) and North America Family Care (-0.5pt) in Q1, and promotion is rising to pre-COVID levels.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q2 organic sales and volume growth, especially North America sell-in versus sell-out, plus share data for Oral Care, Skin Care and Family Care. Organic above 3% with a consumption match supports the bull case.

key_debates.question: Can P&G hold margins and the EPS guide through a first-half-weighted $1.4B cost headwind?

bull.text: Q1 core EPS beat by about $0.12 against a guided decline, even with gross margin down 160bp. Manufacturing productivity added 120bp, SG&A fell 90bp as a share of sales, and half of the headcount reduction is done. Management held core EPS guidance despite raising the commodity headwind.

bear.text: Commodities cost 140bp of Q1 gross margin and most of the cost impact lands in the first half. Tariff recoveries (50bp) may not repeat. Interest costs rise with $4.0B of 5%-plus notes, and Colgate and Kimberly-Clark both flag oil-linked inflation. The guide still needs about +2% core EPS growth over the last three quarters.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q2 gross margin bridge (commodity versus productivity versus pricing), whether FY guidance is held, and whether the Q2 EPS beat comes from operations or from below-the-line items.

key_debates.question: Is Q2 consensus (revenue +5.8%, EPS +5.6%) set too high or too low?

bull.text: Q1 beat revenue consensus by about 2.5% and core EPS by about 6%. Thorne adds revenue from Q2. Earnings estimates did not move after the beat, so numbers may be stale.

bear.text: +5.8% consensus-implied revenue growth is above the top of the FY27 organic guidance (3%) and above the top of the all-in guidance (2-4%, which includes Thorne). Consensus EPS of $1.88 is +5.6% on last year's $1.78 diluted EPS, while FY27 guidance is for core EPS growth of 0% to 3%. Costs and interest rise in the first half.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Thorne's revenue contribution and whether consensus is core or GAAP, plus Q2 organic growth and gross margin. The Investor Day on Nov 19 may reset expectations before the print.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Q2 organic growth holds near 4% as US interventions and China share gains build. Productivity and SG&A leverage offset commodities, and core EPS is at or above the $1.88 consensus with FY guidance raised toward the upper half. This would repeat Q1, when core EPS beat by about $0.12 and the stock rose about 6%.

triggers: Organic sales growth at or above 3.5% with volume positive
Gross margin decline narrower than Q1's 160bp
FY organic or core EPS guidance raised

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Organic growth slows to about 2-3% as Q1 timing and any restocking fade. Gross margin is down again on peak first-half costs and lower tariff help, partly offset by productivity. Core EPS lands around $1.88-1.95, near consensus. Revenue of about $23.0-23.5B includes Thorne, and FY guidance is held.

triggers: FY guidance held and costs described as first-half peak

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Retailer destocking, softer US demand and promotion push organic growth to about 1-2%. Commodity and freight costs and higher interest squeeze margins. EPS misses the $1.88 consensus, and guidance moves to the low end of the range. A Gillette impairment during the December annual test would hit GAAP results.

triggers: North America organic sales negative again
Share losses in Family Care, Oral Care and Skin Care

claim.text: The input-cost headwind is larger and still mostly ahead. The commodity, energy and transport headwind was raised to about $1.4B after tax from about $1B. It is tied to Middle East oil, assuming Brent near $90, and is first-half weighted. Commodities cost 140bp of Q1 gross margin, and management says guidance uncertainty comes from oil and consumer strength.

Debt and funding costs are rising. Debt due within one year was $17.0B at Sept 30 (up from $11.3B at June 30), and $4.0B of 5.1-5.9% notes closed Oct 30 against a 3.3% weighted average on existing debt. Buybacks are partly debt-financed, and the $4.8B 364-day credit facility was due to expire in October 2026. The renewal is not confirmed in our sources.

Thorne ($3.9B, vitamins and supplements) enters the Personal Health Care segment in Q2, financed with debt. The 10-Q calls it not material to results, and purchase accounting is not complete. The acquisition adds goodwill and intangibles and interest cost, with limited near-term earnings help.

The Gillette indefinite-lived intangible ($12.8B carrying value) had fair value above carrying value by only more than 10% at the last test. Isolated sensitivities are -5% (discount rate +25bp), -5% (growth -25bp) and -4% (royalty -50bp), which sum to more than 10%. The annual test falls in the December quarter. Higher interest rates (new notes at up to 5.9%) work against the discount-rate input.

Trade and demand volatility. In Q4, North America sell-in was -1% against consumption of +2% (Prime Day timing, destocking). Management expects trade inventory volatility to continue and promotion is returning to pre-COVID levels. Category growth in North America and focus Europe has slowed 1-2 points, China's market is down about 2%, and Colgate and Kimberly-Clark report soft US volume.

Q1 earnings quality. Tariff costs and recoveries gave 50bp of gross margin, and about half of roughly $200M of IEEPA tariffs paid had been recognized as recoverable by Q4. Q1 operating cash flow included a $1.15B payables inflow, with about $6.5B of payables in supply-chain finance. Both flatter results and may not repeat.

questions_for_management.question: Q1 core EPS rose 1% against your guide of down 5% or more. How much of the gap came from timing, retailer restocking, tariff recoveries or cost phasing, and does that change the Q2 shape?

why.text: Management guided Q1 EPS down 5% or more, and actual was +1%. The 10-Q does not explain the gap, and the answer determines whether Q2 consensus of $1.88 is conservative.

questions_for_management.question: How much of Q1's 2.4% volume and 4.0% organic growth was retailer inventory rebuild after Q4 destocking, and what is the underlying growth rate?

why.text: Q4 sell-in was -1% against consumption of +2% and guidance is only 1-3%, so Q1's 4.0% may include timing that reverses.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Q2 commodity and freight cost impact, and why did the headwind rise to $1.4B while core EPS guidance was held? Which offsets absorbed the extra $0.4B?

why.text: The headwind rose from about $1B to $1.4B with no change to EPS guidance, and the cost is first-half weighted.

questions_for_management.question: How much IEEPA tariff recovery remains to be recognized, and how much of the 50bp Q1 gross margin benefit recurs?

why.text: About half of the roughly $200M was recognized in Q4, and Q1 gross margin received 50bp from lower tariff costs and recoveries.

questions_for_management.question: What revenue, margin and interest cost does Thorne add in Q2 and for the full year, and how much of the 2-4% all-in guide comes from it?

why.text: Thorne's results are called not material but the all-in sales range was raised a full point. Consensus Q2 revenue of $23.50B implies growth above the top of organic guidance.

questions_for_management.question: What is the plan for the Gillette test in the December quarter given the thin cushion, and how do higher interest rates affect the discount rate?

why.text: Fair value exceeded carrying value by only more than 10%, with isolated sensitivities summing to about 14%.

questions_for_management.question: Capex was 5.9% of sales in Q1 against a 4.5-5.5% full-year range. Is the range intact, and how does the 85-90% FCF productivity guide treat the payables inflow and supply-chain finance?

why.text: Q1 capex ran above the guided range and Q1 conversion of 93% benefited from payables.

questions_for_management.question: Where are the remaining share gaps (Oral Care, Skin Care, Family Care, Crest in China), and what changes are planned before the Nov 19 Investor Day?

why.text: Q1 share fell in Oral Care (-0.6pt), Skin Care (-0.6pt) and North America Family Care (-0.5pt), and management said it is deciding what to do in Crest in China.

data_gaps: Whether the $1.88 Q2 consensus EPS is core or GAAP, and the Q2 FY26 core EPS base. Only GAAP diluted EPS ($1.78) is in the sources, so the +5.6% implied growth may not be like-for-like.
Thorne revenue, margin and purchase accounting. The 10-Q says only that results are not material and the allocation is incomplete.

Full text of the Oct 22 earnings release and slides. Only press snippets were available, so the reconciliation of the $0.56 versus $0.79 per share headwind and the quarterly EPS phasing is unconfirmed.
North America and regional organic growth for Q1 FY27, and any evidence of retailer restocking. The 10-Q does not give either.
Whisper EPS, options-implied move, beat/miss history and analyst price targets from structured sources. The only move data is the average closing move of about 2.2% over 8 reports.
Remaining IEEPA tariff recovery amount and timing.
Whether the 364-day $4.8B credit facility due October 2026 has been renewed.
Kimberly-Clark's official Q3 results. Only a secondary news summary of preliminary results was available.
Content of the Nov 19 Investor Day, which falls before the report and may change guidance or targets.
Q2 FY26 segment and organic sales comparatives for the December quarter, and quarterly phasing of the restructuring charges.
